record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Multiple attachments in super-linear preferential attachment
record.original_question: In the super-linear preferential attachment with fitness model, replace the tree growth rule by a multigraph rule in which each new vertex n, at every step n >= 2, chooses m >= 2 existing vertices from T_{n-1} to connect with. How does allowing m multiple attachments per arriving vertex change the phase transition between infinite-star behavior and infinite-path behavior?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8 If at every step n ≥ 2, vertex n were to choose m ≥ 2 many vertices from Tn−1 to connect with, creating a multigraph rather than a tree, how would this influence the phase transition?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following random multigraph growth process with fitness. Let $(F_v)_{v\ge 1}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of strictly positive random variables (the fitnesses) drawn from a fixed distribution $\mu$ on $(0,\infty)$, and let $f:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\to(0,\infty)$ be a super-linear weight function, i.e. $f(k)/k\to\infty$ as $k\to\infty$ (a canonical choice is $f(k)=(k+1)^p$ with $p>1$). Fix an integer $m\ge 2$. Build a sequence of multigraphs $(G_n)_{n\ge 1}$ as follows.
- $G_1$ consists of a single vertex labeled $1$ with fitness $F_1$.
- At each step $n\ge 2$, a new vertex $n$ with fitness $F_n$ is added, and independently (with replacement) $m$ vertices $v_1,\dots,v_m\in\{1,\dots,n-1\}$ are chosen, where each $v_i=u$ is selected with probability proportional to $F_u\,f(\deg_{G_{n-1}}(u))$. Then $m$ edges $\{n,v_1\},\dots,\{n,v_m\}$ are added (possibly with repetitions, yielding a multigraph rather than a tree).

Let $G_\infty=\bigcup_n G_n$ be the limiting multigraph. Determine the almost-sure asymptotic structure of $G_\infty$, and in particular describe the phase diagram (as a function of $f$, $\mu$, and $m$) for the dichotomy between:
(i) the "infinite star" regime, in which there exists a (possibly random) finite set of vertices whose degrees diverge while all but finitely many other vertices have bounded degree; and
(ii) the "infinite path/locally finite" regime, in which every vertex has finite degree almost surely.

Specifically, identify the critical thresholds on $f$ and $\mu$ that separate these regimes when $m\ge 2$, and compare them with the known thresholds in the tree case $m=1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature establishes phase transitions in super-linear preferential attachment trees (Oliveira–Spencer, and additive-fitness models) and separately studies multigraph variants approaching the Rado multigraph, but no source directly resolves how allowing m≥2 multiple attachments per arriving vertex modifies the infinite-star vs. infinite-path phase transition in the super-linear preferential attachment with fitness model. The problem appears to be still open.

status_evidence.title: Connectivity transitions in networks with super-linear preferential attachment
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes super-linear case p>1 in the tree model, characterizing the limiting tree as having one vertex with infinite degree plus finitely many high-degree vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the infinite-star phase transition in the tree (m=1) case but does not address m≥2 multigraphs.

status_evidence.title: Preferential Attachment Processes Approaching The Rado Multigraph
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multigraph preferential attachment with multiple edges per step but in the linear/sublinear setting converging to the Rado multigraph.
status_evidence.claim: Multigraph PA models are studied in different regimes, but not the super-linear-with-fitness phase transition.

status_evidence.title: A phase transition for preferential attachment models with additive fitness
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies a phase transition in PA with additive fitness in the tree case.
status_evidence.claim: Fitness-driven phase transitions are known for trees; multi-attachment extension is not resolved.
